topology: R1/R2 form enterprise AS65001; R3/R4 form provider AS65002. Two iBGP and two eBGP pairs use directly connected peers. PC1 attaches to R1, PC2 to R2, and the HTTP server to R4. iBGP next-hop-self and community transmission are prepared. R4 has a defined but unbound prefix/community import policy. No IGP, static routes or loopbacks substitute for BGP forwarding.
implemented: Thirty-fifth ENARSI entry, in Layer 3 Technologies, with independent practice/reference attempts, a seven-row addressing plan, twenty typed objectives, ordinary IOS/Windows commands and current-domain/path/query share links. Existing UI, icons, terminal styling and offline single HTML are preserved.

Three observed stages: default local external service exits, service-specific LOCAL_PREF200 imported at R2 and propagated through iBGP, then prefix-specific AS-path prepending on the R2 PC1 export. Final PC1 egress is R2 while ingress is R1; PC2 egress/ingress remain R2. R1 installs the service at AD200 and R2 at AD20.

Six traffic directions require three unique original requests each, accepted destination requests and correlated successful replies. Every forwarding hop is matched against the current BGP/connected FIB and delivered physical frames. Enterprise/provider boundary crossings are checked separately on requests and replies, including both client-to-client controls. HTTP requires both complete client responses and observed request/response boundary ports.

Seven reversible exercises: R1-only weight300; equal-AS MED0 versus100; one-AS MED200 winning before a three-AS MED0 candidate; configured community without delivery followed by send-community; received tag followed by matched provider policy setting LP250; inbound rejection of the preferred service with retained raw advertisements; and shutdown/recovery of the R2 external edge. Each needs working alternate forwarding and both HTTP responses, then fresh restored six-direction traffic.

The MED exercise requires observed equal-path preparation. Community delivery requires observed tag-without-send preparation, and provider-policy credit requires a fresh received-tag/unbound-policy observation. A community alone does not change preference; LP250 from matched policy makes the longer path win on both provider routers, while the control prefix retains LP100.

Eight directed peer views receive actual TCP179 OPEN/KEEPALIVE/UPDATE. Soft policy changes preserve transport identities. A loss-injected test verifies that a changed outbound prepend reaches the remote raw table only after real TCP delivery resumes. Physical failover leaves six Established peer views, with both iBGP pairs retained, and moves both client directions to R1.

Seven live and thirteen observed checks: practice0, observed baseline1, local preference2, restored core13, complete20; reference7 with no pre-earned observations. Quiet completed stages avoid rescanning packet history. Configuration-only toggles, stale traffic, missing directions, incomplete HTTP and omitted preparation observations cannot earn exercise credit. Earned history survives YAML reopen while runtime state rebuilds.

Rendered IOS replay, hard clear, saved reload, published verification commands, route-map help/Tab, transactional rejection of invalid attribute values, saved startup equality and invalid/foreign criterion rejection are covered. This lab reuses existing working BGP/TCP/IP mechanisms; no simulation-engine, CLI-parser or terminal-style changes were required.
scope: IPv4 unicast BGP enterprise/provider path policy with IOS routers. Cisco primary documentation reviewed; no fresh CML capture or universal IOS/NX-OS protocol equivalence is claimed.
